name: AI Pet Dance Generator
blurb: One photo of your cat or dog, and it stands up and dances.

prompts.label: Template prompt
prompts.text: One to three reference photos, one pet each: a cat, a dog or any animal. Keep every pet exactly as photographed: same species, breed, fur colour, markings, eyes and ears, and never swap them. Set the dance in the place from the first photo, same room or garden, same light. Their whole bodies stay in frame from ears to paws the whole time, camera static at their eye level a couple of metres away. (1) The pets rise up onto their hind legs and start bouncing to the beat; (2) they sway side to side and swing their front paws across their bodies, heads bobbing; (3) they turn once on the spot and shake their tails at the camera; (4) they spin back round, step toward the lens and finish with both front paws up in the air. With two or three pets, they dance side by side in sync. Real animal anatomy: paws, never human hands, natural fur. One continuous shot, vertical 9:16. Upbeat, bouncy pop beat in the audio, no vocals. No people, no text, no logos, no watermark.

prompts.text: One to three reference photos, one pet each; keep every pet exactly as photographed: same species, breed, fur colour and face, and never swap them. With one photo, that one pet dances alone in the middle of the studio. Real animal anatomy: paws, never human hands. One continuous shot, vertical 9:16. Upbeat dance-pop beat in the audio, no vocals. No people, no text, no logos, no watermark.

prompts.text: One reference photo of a pet; keep it exactly as photographed: same species, breed, fur colour, markings and face. Dress it in a bright yellow hooded raincoat and small yellow rain boots. It stands in a wide puddle on a wet city pavement on a rainy autumn day, fallen leaves in the water, a few people with umbrellas blurred far behind. Its whole body stays in frame the whole time, camera static at its eye level. (1) It rises onto its hind legs and stamps its boots in the puddle to the beat, ripples spreading; (2) it turns round with its hood up and its tail swishing out from under the coat; (3) it spins back to face the camera, swings its front paws side to side and does a little hop; (4) it finishes with one paw raised, looking into the lens. Real animal anatomy: paws, never human hands. One continuous shot, vertical 9:16. Light rain and a bouncy pop beat in the audio, no vocals. No text, no logos, no watermark.
